name: White Star Capital
identity_check: Confirmed as White Star Capital (whitestarcapital.com), which calls itself a global multi-stage technology investment firm, co-founded by managing partners Eric Martineau-Fortin and Jean-Francois Marcoux. Its own Medium blog (whitestarcapital.medium.com, linked from the site's Perspectives page) announced the $250M Fund IV close on 5 Aug 2026, confirming the user-list lead ('Q3 2026 fund close $250M'). The site lists offices in London, New York, Montreal, Paris, Toronto, Guernsey, Berlin, Milan and Abu Dhabi but names no headquarters. Its LinkedIn company page, linked from the site, gives London (W1T postcode) as headquarters, so London is used. BetaKit says it is headquartered in the UK and New York. Fund vehicles found: three earlier flagship funds (White Star Capital I–III), Fund IV (Series A–B), a North American Seed Fund (pre-seed and seed) and two Digital Asset Funds (crypto). Tokyo is not a current office: it appears only in a 2021 press release and in the location of a Tokyo/Seoul venture partner. Founder bios and LinkedIn give earlier founding dates (2007, 2008); see conflicts. Not to be confused with unrelated businesses that use the White Star name.

thesis_text.value: Global multi-stage technology investor, founded in 2014, that leads and co-leads rounds for founders aiming to scale internationally. Its core Fund IV backs Series A and B; a North American Seed Fund leads pre-seed and seed rounds in Canada and the US; a separate digital-asset strategy backs crypto companies. Current themes include AI models, vertical AI and physical AI.

open_items: SEC EDGAR returned 403 to the 'CapitalAtlas research' User-Agent, so Form D filings for White Star fund entities were not checked.
Fund IV's initial ticket size is not published. check_max_usd ($20M) is the initial-ticket ceiling of Fund III (2021), and check_min_usd ($0.5M) is the North American Seed Fund's minimum lead check.
North American Seed Fund final close not found; only the $25M first close (Sep 2025) against a $50M target. The Fund IV post (Aug 2026) mentions the Seed Fund but gives no size.
Digital Asset Fund II: the $120M is the fund size stated at the first-close announcement (Apr 2022); the first-close amount and any final close were not found.
Indian founders: nothing stated on any page. Sanjay Zimmermann focuses on Canada and Southeast Asia, and no India strategy is mentioned.
Autonomique seed amount is undisclosed, and its founding year is not on the fetched pages. The Robot Report calls it Menlo Park-based with a Montreal office; White Star lists it as California, USA.
Tetrix: White Star says it is co-leading, but the other co-lead is not named on the fetched pages (the Axios article is paywalled past the first paragraph).

FluxCo: only The SaaS News page was fetched. The WSJ article (linked from White Star's newsroom, 23 Jul 2026) is paywalled. One aggregator calls the round a Series A; this is unconfirmed, so 'Seed' is kept. Founding year not found.

Veesion: the Le Monde du Droit deal note names Red River West, Bpifrance, KPN and existing investors (Odyssée Venture, Verve Ventures, Founders Future) without roles, so they are recorded as unspecified. Only White Star's site says White Star led.

Vention Series D (US$110M, 27 Jan 2026) appears in White Star's portfolio news, but neither BetaKit nor the press release names White Star in the round (Investissement Québec led), so it is not recorded. White Star is an earlier Vention investor.

Not recorded because White Star's role was not confirmed on a fetched page: Sequen Series B ($90M, Sep 2026, led by Prysm Capital; Axios paywalled), Spiko Series B ($90M, Oct 2026, led by NEA), Finn Series D (€140M, Jun 2026), Cata seed ($5.3M, Apr 2026), Kulipa seed ($6.2M, Apr 2026) and Alfred Pay Series A ($15M, Jan 2026).
